Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Next steps: POC scope & SDK compatibility — VentureHealth

Hi Aarti / Maya — thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of pain points you described:
- Latency spikes in batch processing of clinical summaries (95th pct spikes above 700ms on current infra).
- High per-request cost with current provider when moving to higher throughput.
- Need for predictable behavior across dev / staging / prod for compliance and QA.

Success criteria you called out:
1) End-to-end throughput: sustain 1k reqs/minute for the summarization job within P95 latency target of <= 200ms for short prompts (<=512 tokens).
2) Cost target: reduce per-1000-token cost by >= 30% versus current provider for inference.
3) Quality: summary ROUGE/QA pass rate >= current baseline (you’ll share a 50-sample eval set).
4) Security/compliance: SOC2 evidence and US data residency for POC logs.

Current stack you said you’re running:
- Backend: Ruby on Rails (primary inference orchestration)
- Workers: Node for async tasks in some services
- Model access: existing managed LLM provider via REST API

POC scope (recommended):
- 3-week POC focused on the summarization pipeline only.
- Integration options: use Redwood hosted API as drop-in via REST; full SDK integration (Python/Node) for the worker prototype.
- Measure latency, cost, and quality on your 50-sample eval set and a representative 1-hour production traffic replay.

Technical compatibility notes / asks for you:
- You mentioned Ruby is your canonical backend. Redwood provides first-class SDKs for Python and Node; Ruby customers commonly call our REST endpoints from Rails with the same set of features (streaming + function/tool calling). Would you be able to run a small Node or Python worker as part of the POC, or prefer we provide a Ruby quickstart?
- Need confirmation on data residency for logs and whether any PHI will be included in POC traces.

Proposed timeline & owners:
- Week of Mar 16: Kickoff + environment access (Redwood: Sergio + Monica; VentureHealth: Maya + engineering lead)
- Week of Mar 23: Integration and baseline measurements (Monica to lead SDK/REST integration)
- Week of Mar 30: Final measurements, evaluation, and decision meeting (Sergio to present results)

Attachments (for your review): VH_POC_MAPlan_v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), redwood_sdk_matrix.csv (SDK feature matrix), SOC2-Summary.pdf (high-level security summary).

Immediate ask / next steps:
- Can you confirm: 1) acceptance of the 3-week scope, 2) whether you want a Ruby quickstart or can run a temporary Node/Python worker, and 3) procurement contact for a simple NDA/statement of work?

If that all looks good I’ll send a formal calendar invite for the kickoff and share the HubSpot deal link for tracking.

Thanks —
Sergio

Thanks Sergio — appreciated the thorough recap. A few clarifying points from our side:

- The success criteria look right; I’ll upload the 50-sample eval set to the shared Drive by EOD Monday.
- On the Ruby question: our inference orchestration is in Rails, and adding a Node/Python worker is doable but would require a short change request. Ideally we’d prefer a Ruby quickstart for speed, but we can make the temporary worker approach work if it speeds the timeline.
- Security: the POC will not include PHI; however, the production rollout will. We need to confirm encryption-at-rest and retention policy for logs during the POC.
- One more technical item: does Redwood’s tokenization differ from common OpenAI tokenizers in a way that could affect cost estimates? We want to avoid surprises on token counts.

If you can confirm Ruby quickstart + tokenization details, we’ll confirm the procurement contact: procurement@venturehealth.com (they’re on copy).

Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Next steps: POC scope & SDK compatibility — VentureHealth (internal)

Looping in quick internal notes so we have an answer ready for Maya:

- SDKs: We have stable Python and Node SDKs with streaming, function-calling, and retry logic. No official Ruby SDK today.
- Ruby path: recommend two options:
  1) Provide a Ruby quickstart repo that demonstrates using our REST API (includes streaming examples and a small token-count helper). I can put this together by Mar 12.
  2) If they prefer a worker, we can supply a Node worker example that plugs into their pipeline; faster for instrumentation but requires a short infra change.
- Tokenization: Redwood uses the same tokenization method we’ve documented (compatibility mode with common BPE tokenizers). Tokenization differences are minor, but we will include a tokenization inspection report for their 50-sample eval set so they can see per-sample token counts before the POC starts.
- Security: SOC2-Summary.pdf covers encryption-at-rest and access controls; retention defaults to 30 days for POC logs but we can sign an SOW amendment if they need shorter retention or additional masking.

I’ll draft the Ruby quickstart and a tokenization report if they confirm they want Ruby. If they pick the temporary worker approach we’ll prioritize the Node example so integration is quicker.

Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
